title: Lesson 36: A Chance in a Million

segments.text: Lesson 36
segments.translation: 第36课

segments.text: A chance in a million
segments.translation: 万分之一的机遇

segments.text: Listen to the tape then answer this question.
segments.translation: 听录音，然后回答问题。

segments.text: What was the chance in a million?
segments.translation: 什么是“万分之一的机遇”？

segments.text: We are less credulous than we used to be.
segments.translation: 我们现在不像以前那样容易轻信了。

segments.text: In the nineteenth century, a novelist would bring his story to a conclusion by presenting his readers with a series of coincidences--most of them wildly improbable.
segments.translation: 在19世纪，小说家往往通过向读者提供一系列巧合来结束他的故事——其中大多数都是极不可能发生的。

segments.text: Readers happily accepted the fact that an obscure maidservant was really the hero's mother.
segments.translation: 读者竟然愉快地接受了这样一个事实：一个卑微的女佣人竟然是男主人公的生母。

segments.text: A long-lost brother, who was presumed dead, was really alive all the time and wickedly plotting to bring about the hero's downfall. And so on.
segments.translation: 一个失散多年、被认为已经死去的兄弟实际上一直活着，并正阴险地策划着让男主人公败落。如此等等。

segments.text: Modern readers would find such naive solutions totally unacceptable.
segments.translation: 现代读者会发现这类天真的解决办法完全无法接受。

segments.text: Yet, in real life, circumstances do sometimes conspire to bring about coincidences which anyone but a nineteenth century novelist would find incredible.
segments.translation: 然而在现实生活中，情况有时确实会凑巧，以致产生出除了19世纪小说家外，谁都会觉得难以置信的巧合。

segments.text: When I was a boy, my grandfather told me how a German taxi driver, Franz Bussman, found a brother who was thought to have been killed twenty years before.
segments.translation: 当我还是个男孩时，我祖父给我讲了一个德国出租车司机 Franz Bussman 是如何找到了他那被认为在20年前就已经阵亡了的兄弟的故事。

segments.text: While on a walking tour with his wife, he stopped to talk to a workman.
segments.translation: 当他正和妻子徒步旅行时，他停下来同一个工人交谈。

segments.text: After they had gone on, Mrs. Bussman commented on the workman's close resemblance to her husband and even suggested that he might be his brother.
segments.translation: 在他们继续往前走之后，Bussman 夫人评论说那个工人长得和她丈夫非常相像，甚至暗示说他可能就是他兄弟。

segments.text: Franz poured scorn on the idea, pointing out that his brother had been killed in action during the war.
segments.translation: Franz 对这种想法嗤之以鼻，指出他的兄弟在战争期间已经阵亡了。

segments.text: Though Mrs. Bussman was fully acquainted with this story, she thought that there was a chance in a million that she might be right.
segments.translation: 虽然 Bussman 夫人非常熟悉这个故事，但她认为有百万分之一的可能性，她或许是对的。

segments.text: A few days later, she sent a boy to the workman to ask him if his name was Hans Bussman.
segments.translation: 几天后，她派了一个男孩去问那个工人他的名字是不是 Hans Bussman。

segments.text: Needless to say, the man's name was Hans Bussman and he really was Franz's long-lost brother.
segments.translation: 不用说，这人的名字正是 Hans Bussman，他确实是 Franz 失散多年的兄弟。

segments.text: When the brothers were reunited, Hans explained how it was that he was still alive.
segments.translation: 当兄弟俩团聚时，Hans 解释了他为何还活着。

segments.text: After having been wounded towards the end of the war, he had been sent to hospital and was separated from his unit.
segments.translation: 他在战争快结束时受了伤，被送进医院并与部队失去了联系。

segments.text: The hospital had been bombed and Hans had made his way back into Western Germany on foot.
segments.translation: 医院遭到了轰炸，Hans 徒步回到了西德。

segments.text: Meanwhile, his unit was lost and all records of him had been destroyed.
segments.translation: 与此同时，他的部队被打散了，他所有的记录都被销毁了。

segments.text: Hans returned to his family home, but the house had been bombed and no one in the neighbourhood knew what had become of the inhabitants.
segments.translation: Hans 回到了他的家，但房子已经被炸毁了，而附近没有人知道居民们的下落。

segments.text: Assuming that his family had been killed during an air raid, Hans settled down in a village fifty miles away where he had remained ever since.
segments.translation: Hans 以为他的家人都在空袭中丧生了，于是在50英里外的一个村庄定居下来，并一直呆在那里至今。
